cf.title: Fix: VACUUM FULL or CREATE INDEX fails with error "missing chunk number 0 for toast value XXX"

input.subject: VACUUM FULL or CREATE INDEX fails with error: missing chunk number 0 for toast value XXX

verdict_reasoning: The bug is reproducible, demand is shown, and no surviving objection questions the goal. Two fixable design points remain. standards-compat-1 asks what the fix reports when a chunk is missing, so that real corruption stays visible. maintenance-fit-1 asks where the tolerant handling lives, since CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK still need it. Both need someone who knows heap visibility and TOAST to sign.

brief.title: Fix missing TOAST chunk errors in CREATE INDEX and VACUUM FULL
brief.problem: CREATE INDEX and VACUUM FULL can fail with "missing chunk number 0 for toast value" when the TOAST table removed chunks of a tuple that the main table still treats as RECENTLY_DEAD. The thread links this to bug #18351, which was reported earlier and not resolved. The error carries SQLSTATE XX001 (data corrupted), so operators with corruption monitoring get false alerts.
brief.proposed_design: The first prototype stores the parent table's OldestXmin in VacuumParams and reuses it when VACUUM processes the TOAST table, so both use the same horizon. Matthias van de Meent replied that on-access pruning and btree index tuple removal can still remove the TOAST data. Michael Paquier then posted, in another thread linked to this CF entry, a patch that detoasts attributes more aggressively during index builds.
author_claims: The bug comes from different horizons: ComputeXidHorizons filters by database, but GetSnapshotData does not.
The OldestXmin prototype fails make check, with freezing cutoffs too far in the past and assertion failures.
A definitely_needed check in CREATE INDEX could slow it down.
Michael Paquier says aggressive detoasting is fine for index builds, which need the detoasted values anyway.
Andrey Borodin says each occurrence triggers corruption alerts in his fleet monitoring.
brief.thread_state: All 7 messages are visible. Discussion moved to a separate thread where Michael Paquier posted an aggressive-detoasting patch for index builds; the CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK paths still need a fix, and the OldestXmin prototype is effectively set aside.
unclear: Which patch the CF entry asks reviewers to review: the OldestXmin prototype, Paquier's detoasting patch, or both.
How the fix will handle copy_for_cluster(), where tuples are copied without detoasting.
Whether a race-caused missing chunk will be skipped silently or reported with a different SQLSTATE than real corruption.
What aggressive detoasting costs for index builds on large toasted columns.
Whether the fix will be back-patched, given the Bugfix tag and target version 20.

objections.title: Skipping tuples with missing TOAST data hides real corruption from CREATE INDEX
objections.failure_scenario: A table has a real lost TOAST chunk on a RECENTLY_DEAD tuple. Today CREATE INDEX or VACUUM FULL stops with XX001, and monitoring alerts. With the skip-on-missing design the command succeeds silently, and the operator learns of the damage only if a later read of a live tuple hits it.
objections.argument: Message #2 proposes ignoring TOAST visibility errors during index builds, and message #3 links a patch based on aggressive detoasting. Message #4 raises the masking concern, and no message answers it. Message #6 shows operators depend on XX001 meaning corruption. The proposal does not say whether a skipped chunk is logged, gets another SQLSTATE, or is limited to tuples the code can prove were removed by the race, and that choice changes what existing monitoring sees after upgrade or a back-patch.
objections.author_must_show: When a RECENTLY_DEAD tuple's TOAST data is missing, what does the fix report, and how does it tell this race apart from real corruption?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 raises the masking concern and no later message answers it. Message #6 shows monitoring depends on XX001, and the visible material does not say what the fix reports when a chunk is missing.

objections.title: Missing-chunk tolerance lives in each caller, so new paths can regress
objections.failure_scenario: Someone later adds or changes a path that reads TOAST data of RECENTLY_DEAD tuples, such as a REPACK variant, a table AM's index build scan, or an extension's rewrite. That path does not repeat the detoast-and-tolerate step, and no test or assertion flags it. Users then get XX001 "missing chunk" errors again, found only through corruption alerts in production.
objections.argument: Message #2 says missing TOAST data is to be expected for RECENTLY_DEAD tuples, so every reader of such tuples must handle it. The fix in message #3 covers only the heap index build. It says CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK need separate, deeper work. The material shows no shared helper or table AM contract, so each table AM and each future maintenance path must find out about this race on its own.
objections.author_must_show: Will the tolerant handling sit in one shared helper or a documented table AM rule that future copy and build paths must use, and what test fails if a path skips it?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 confirms the fix covers only index builds and that CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK need separate work, so at least two paths need the same handling. The table AM and extension part is speculative, because other AMs manage their own TOAST storage.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The prototype adds fields to VacuumParams in vacuum.h, and the detoasting fix changes what the heap index build scan passes to callbacks.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix and the bug reproduces on 17.10, but the target version is 20.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each path that reads TOAST data of RECENTLY_DEAD tuples needs the tolerant handling, and CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK are not yet covered.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Aggressive detoasting runs in every index build scan, and its cost on large toasted columns is not shown.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: When a RECENTLY_DEAD tuple's TOAST data is missing, what does the fix report, and how does it tell this race apart from real corruption?
Will the tolerant handling sit in one shared helper that index build, CLUSTER, VACUUM FULL and REPACK all use, and what test fails if a path skips it?
How will copy_for_cluster() handle a RECENTLY_DEAD tuple whose external TOAST value is copied by reference and is already gone?
Which patch should reviewers of this CF entry read: the OldestXmin prototype, the aggressive-detoasting patch, or both?
Will the fix be back-patched to the supported branches where the bug reproduces, and does it change any struct or callback that extensions use?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier is listed as author and posted the detoasting patch in message #3. The owner must know heap visibility horizons, TOAST access and the table rewrite code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the rule that missing TOAST data of RECENTLY_DEAD tuples is tolerated without hiding real corruption, in every maintenance path and in each back-patched branch, for as long as those branches are supported.
committability.author_follow_up: Michael Paquier attached his patch thread to this entry in July and set the target version. The entry has needed a rebase since 2026-10-17, and the VACUUM FULL part has no patch yet.

priority.reason: The race raises XX001 corruption alerts in a production fleet and was reported twice, so the fix has clear value. The detoasting patch was not read; it touches heap index builds, and the rewrite paths still need a design.

provisional_note: The aggressive-detoasting patch is in another thread and was not read. Its error reporting, its cost on wide toasted columns and its effect on the table AM interface could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support for 8-byte TOAST values (aka the TOAST infinite loop problem)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set lets TOAST tables use 8-byte value IDs (a new oid8 type, a wider OID counter, a reloption and a new on-disk vartag) so that TOAST tables are no longer limited to about 4 billion values. It also adds a toast_external layer that converts on-disk external TOAST pointers to an in-memory struct through per-vartag callbacks, so that more vartags, such as for zstd, can be added later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The toast_external layer with function pointer redirection got no support. Tom Lane questioned its run-time cost and called it overdesigned, and the author later said the design had not received a single +1. Only the oid8 data type was committed. The author then dropped the rest from the v19 cycle, planning a v20 rework without the redirections.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Anyway, as far as things stand today on this thread, I have not been able to get even a single +1 for this design.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refuse setting toast.* reloptions when TOAST relation does not exist
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes setting or changing a toast.* reloption raise an error when the table has no TOAST relation. Today such a value is accepted and then lost, so pg_dump does not keep it and it has no effect if toastable columns are added later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas pointed out that the rules for whether a table gets a TOAST table can change between major releases, so a pg_dump and restore of a table with a toast.* option could fail after an upgrade. Tom Lane added that the choice can differ on different hardware and opposed a hard error, though a warning might be acceptable. The CF manager returned the patch because there was no consensus on whether it was useful or correct; alternatives such as creating the TOAST relation when a toast.* option is set were left for a new patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If a table with that
definition has a toast.* option set, then upgrading from release X to
release X+1 via pg_dump and restore will fail.  That's bad.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add MAIN_RELATION_CLEANUP and TOAST_TABLE_CLEANUP options to VACUUM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two VACUUM options, MAIN_RELATION_CLEANUP and TOAST_TABLE_CLEANUP (first named SECONDARY_RELATION_CLEANUP), so a table owner can vacuum only the main relation or only its TOAST table. It reuses VACOPT_SKIPTOAST, adds a flag to vacuum_rel() to skip the main relation, and adds matching vacuumdb support.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers questioned whether the use case justifies new options and more complex vacuum code. A TOAST table can already be vacuumed directly by name, with GRANT USAGE ON pg_toast for unprivileged roles, or through a script or SQL function. Michael Paquier suggested exposing only VACOPT_SKIPTOAST to users, and the entry was returned with feedback after no further activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am not sure that this use-case justifies a new option and more complications in the code paths of vacuum though.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoiding deadlock errors in CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the third wait in create index concurrently, the wait for transactions with older snapshots at the end of phase 3, so that concurrent DDL on the same table no longer fails with deadlock errors. It sets indcheckxmin when the index is marked ready and makes pg_index updates transactional so older snapshots cannot use the new index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was returned with feedback for lack of activity after it had waited on the author for more than two weeks. Michael Paquier doubted that the transactional pg_index update is safe and asked whether all cache lookup failures were fixed. Yoshikazu Imai pointed to comments describing the create index concurrently method that need changes, and the visible messages show no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And while looking at this patch, I have doubts that what you are doing
is actually safe either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Full support for index LP_DEAD hint bits on standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let index scans on a hot standby use and set index LP_DEAD hint bits, which are currently ignored during recovery. The first design added a WAL record carrying a hint-bit xmin horizon tied to hot_standby_feedback; it was later reworked to mask primary-set hint bits in full-page images and let the standby set its own bits only when minRecoveryPoint makes it safe.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Late in the cycle Peter Geoghegan reviewed the patch; his review is visible only as quoted in the author's reply. He questioned whether the lockless algorithm using pg_memory_barrier() was correct, pointed out a problem with LP_DEAD bits on posting lists during posting list splits, and said the patch had serious design flaws. In his visible message he said the area carries a real risk of hidden data corruption bugs, that few committers could evaluate such a patch, and that the problem needed better explanation. A test added by the patch was also failing intermittently, and the author moved the entry back to Waiting on Author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
You must understand that this whole area is *scary*. The potential for
serious data corruption bugs is very real.

precedents_retrieved.title: create index failed. PARALLEL UNSAFE function does not prevent parallel index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made plan_create_index_workers() check parallel safety on the raw index expressions and predicate, read from the pg_index syscache, so that a PARALLEL UNSAFE function folded to a constant still prevents a parallel index build. The bug report showed CREATE INDEX failing in a parallel worker because a plpgsql function with an EXCEPTION block was const-folded before the check.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed and then reverted after Tom Lane objected. He said it does not fix the failure, which returns when the function is marked PARALLEL SAFE, and that it breaks the planner rule that original markings stop mattering once a function is inlined or const-folded. He also said that passing raw parse-analysis output to is_parallel_safe() misses parallel-unsafe default arguments, and he preferred making exception-using functions parallel safe through a separate commitfest patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's a band-aid
that doesn't really solve the problem: if I simply declare the
function as PARALLEL SAFE, the failure comes right back.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pluggable toaster
precedents_retrieved.authors: Fedor Sigaev (sigaev), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Oleg Bartunov (oleg), Nikita Malakhov (nmalakh)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Matthias van de Meent, Aleksander Alekseev
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds a toaster API, like the table AM API, so extensions can plug in custom toasters per column, with new SQL syntax and a custom toast pointer format, and routes the built-in toaster through it. Later revisions moved toaster assignments into a new catalog pg_toastrel, added DROP TOASTER, and planned a hooks-based extension version.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patches add a lot of code and complexity without fixing any TOAST problem, and said he would not accept the planned hooks either. Matthias van de Meent and Aleksander Alekseev said a complex design was posted before there was community agreement on how type-aware TOAST should work, and asked for that design discussion first. Aleksander Alekseev also cited maintenance cost and benchmarks that others could not reproduce, and moved the discussion to the compression dictionaries thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The problem for me is that what you've been posting doesn't actually fix any problem, but instead introduces lots of new code and complexity.

precedents_retrieved.title: Doc: Fix definition of asynchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites one sentence in the log-shipping standby docs that says WAL records are shipped after transaction commit. The new text says log shipping is asynchronous by default, meaning the primary does not wait for the standby to receive the data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers agreed the sentence is wrong but proposed other wordings, and Robert Treat argued the section should only cover file-based log shipping. Michael Paquier doubted the one-sentence fix was worth applying alone, because the whole section mixes file-based shipping and streaming and needs reorganizing. The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am not sure if this is worth applying on its own, TBH, because this stuff needs much more rework than a simple sentence.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
Reverted commit(s): Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
Reverted commit(s): Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4", when available
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 7c1849311e49, due to the fact that more than 60% of
the buildfarm members do not have lz4 installed.  As we are in the last
commit fest of the development cycle, and that it could take a couple
of weeks to stabilize things, this change is reverted for now.

This commit will be reworked in a lighter version, as
default_toast_compression's default can be changed to "lz4" without the
switch from --with-lz4 to --without-lz4.  This approach will keep the
buildfarm at bay, and still allow builds to take advantage of LZ4 in
TOAST by default, as long as the code is compiled with LZ4 support.

A harder requirement based on LZ4 should be achievable at some point,
but it is going to require some work from the buildfarm owners first.
Perhaps this part could be revisited at the beginning of the next
development cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. Message #1 says bug #18351 was reported earlier but not resolved, without giving a reason that could be weighed here. Matthias van de Meent rejected the OldestXmin prototype in message #2, and the discussion then moved to the aggressive-detoasting patch, so no earlier rejection reason applies to the current approach.
The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or psql change. The only contract issue in this angle is how errors are reported, covered above.

No on-disk format, WAL, catalog or wire protocol change is proposed. The set-aside prototype only adds VacuumParams fields, and the open questions about copy_for_cluster() and back-patch ABI cannot be judged without the detoasting patch's interface.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect: it changes no privilege, role, default or visible data, and CREATE INDEX and VACUUM FULL keep their ownership checks. Skipping a missing chunk could hide real corruption, but message #4 already raises that, and it is an integrity question for another angle.

The bug fix is plainly desirable, and the people working on it know the area: a committer wrote the current patch, and two experienced reviewers are engaged. Without the detoasting patch I could not check its cost for wide toasted columns or its effect on the table AM interface.

This is a bug fix for a race that makes CREATE INDEX and VACUUM FULL fail with an XX001 error. No existing feature, setting or extension prevents it, and the allowlist workaround in message #6 does not fix the race. Other angles cover design gaps, such as copy_for_cluster() and possible masking of real corruption.

Demand is shown. This is a bug fix for a reproducible error first reported as bug #18351 and reported again in a second thread (message #7). Message #6 describes a production fleet whose corruption monitoring pages operators on each occurrence, and several committers and reviewers are engaged.
